newsitem.title: USA: U.S. congressional delegation visits China.
newsitem.headline: U.S. congressional delegation visits China.

text.p: A U.S. Congressional delegation was due to arrive in Hong Kong on Friday as part of a fact-finding trip on China ahead of an annual debate by lawmakers on trade relations with Beijing.

The 22-member House delegation is being led by Rep. Jim Kolbe, R-Az. In a statement issued before the group left Washington on Wednesday, Kolbe said it was time for Congress "to forge a more coherent, bipartisan policy towards China."

Each year, the president and Congress have to decide whether to renew China's Most Favored Nation trade status. Human rights, nuclear proliferation, protection of U.S. copyrights and the huge U.S. trade deficit with China are factors in the annual debate.
In recent years U.S. businesses have been lobbying lawmakers to end the yearly ritual over U.S.-China trade relations and grant permanent MFN.

"This process has been more divisive than productive and thus has not enabled Congress to effectively influence the behavior of the Chinese government," Kolbe said. "We must move beyond this annual, destructive debate."

But some trade analysts and Clinton administration officials believe the time is not right to deal with the question of permanent MFN for China and that it would be better to deal with China's entry into the World Trade Organization first.

Kolbe said the delegation, comprised of an equal number of Republicans and Democrats representing 15 states, will explore a wide range of issues, including Hong Kong's handover to China in July and economic and trade issues.
The group will meet business and Chinese officials in Beijing, tour an aircraft facility in Xian and meet business leaders and hold a press conference in Shanghai.
